title: Creating Custom Input Components
description: Build reusable form components that support v-model.

slides.title: Custom Input with v-model
slides.content:
# Implementing v-model on a Component

To make a custom component work with `v-model`, it must:
- Accept a `modelValue` prop.
- Emit an `update:modelValue` event with the new value.

```javascript
// CustomInput.vue
export default {
  props: ['modelValue'],
  emits: ['update:modelValue'],
  template: `
    <input 
      :value="modelValue"
      @input="$emit('update:modelValue', $event.target.value)"
    >
  `
}
```

Then use it: `<CustomInput v-model="text" />`

slides.title: Multiple v-model Bindings
slides.content:
# v-model with Arguments

For components that need multiple two‑way bindings, you can use `v-model:propName`.

```html
<CustomForm v-model:firstName="first" v-model:lastName="last" />
```

Inside the component, accept `firstName` and `lastName` as props, and emit `update:firstName`, `update:lastName`.

quizData.question: What does a custom component need to support `v-model`?
quizData.explanation: In Vue 3, the default contract is a `modelValue` prop and an `update:modelValue` event. Vue 2 used `value` and `input`.
